steps.name: Probability Independence (Anti-Circularity)
steps.detail: Given Duel's committed multiplier table (kenoConfig.json), independently-derived hypergeometric probabilities P(k) = C(picks,k)×C(40-picks,10-k)/C(40,10) yield 99.9% RTP for all 40 configurations (analytic identity over the full table). Max deviation: 0.000000% (CLASSIC/picks=2 (RTP=99.900000%)). The hit probabilities are derived independently from the RNG analysis; the multiplier table is operator-supplied. Live play (Step 8) exercised 190/260 table rows and matched every captured payout; rare high-hit rows that did not occur in the 5,100-bet sample are evaluated against the committed table via this identity rather than empirically.

informational.label: RTP Analysis
informational.detail: Empirical RTP: 91.39% over 5,100 bets (high variance at this sample size; theoretical 99.90% proven analytically in Step 16)

informational.label: Chi-squared Goodness-of-Fit
informational.detail: 40 configs; fails at α=0.01: 0/40; min p=0.1168 (~128 bets/config insufficient; see simulation Step 19)

informational.label: Serial Independence (lag-1)
informational.detail: r₁=0.320, z=22.85 — large z is expected: the dataset contains Phase B (1,000 consecutive picks=1 bets, E[hits]=0.25) followed by Phase C (1,000 consecutive picks=10 bets, E[hits]=2.5). This regime shift creates artificial serial correlation in the aggregate hit series. It is a property of the audit's phase ordering, not the RNG. Simulation Step 19 tests each config independently at 1M rounds and finds 0/40 serial independence failures.

informational.label: Serial Independence (runs test)
informational.detail: runs=1519, expected=2097.0, z=-19.70, p=0.00e+0 — same phase-ordering artifact as lag-1 above (picks=1 → picks=10 regime shift). Per-config simulation in Step 19 confirms RNG outputs are serially independent.
